maya: Quick heads-up — saw a surprising NDCG hit after landing quantized reranker v2 on shadowbench :confused:
maya: Baseline float32 NDCG@10=0.421, quantized int8 NDCG@10=0.392 (same candidate pool, same seed)
maya: MRR hardly moved (0.232 -> 0.229) so it's very wedge-y on tail ordering
maya: Repro steps: ran nightly shadowbench job with the usual sample cohort, command below:
maya: ```
./run_rerank_eval --model rerank-v2-int8 --candidates /mnt/eval/cands.jsonl --seed 42 --metric ndcg@10 --cohort cohortA
```
maya: Noticed this only when candidates are passed in original doc order (doc anchor first) — if we shuffle candidates prior to scoring the delta reduces to ~0.008
sam: Interesting. Could be quantization interacting with positional kvpack or attention op ordering. Any tokenizer or priming changes?
maya: No tokenizer change. But we do prefix a short priming template for each query ("Search results for: <query>\n") — toggling that off reduces the gap a bit
lee: Could be numeric underflow in KV cache on certain sequence alignments. Which runtime flags were used?
maya: Default runtime flags. We haven't disabled prefix_cache or streaming.
maya: Quick sample failing pair (query + two top candidates):
maya: ```
Q: "how to reset oauth token for service x"
C1 (ranked higher in float): "service x oauth reset - step by step"
C2 (ranked higher in quant): "oauth token rotate service x"
```
maya: Both look semantically comparable, but quantized model prefers the terser phrasing for some reason
sam: Can you run with --disable-prefix-cache and --no-kvpack to isolate? Also retest with batch_size=1 vs 8
maya: Will run now on a small sample and post results in 15m
olivia: FWIW, shadowbench cohortA is enriched for long anchors — maybe length interacts with quantized attention scaling
lee: I can spin up a dedicated float/quant parity job on a single GPU so infra noise is minimal. Want me to run float32 and int8 back-to-back on same node?
maya: Yes please. Also add a run with priming removed and one where we left-pad query with a neutral token so alignment changes
sam: Also try toggling tokenizer normalization (casefold) — last time a mismatch there caused weird tie-breaking
maya: Quick smoke results (local sample 100q):
- float32 NDCG@10 0.4209
- int8 NDCG@10 0.3941
- int8 with shuffle candidates 0.4130
- int8 no-priming 0.4087
- int8 disable-prefix-cache 0.4165

maya: So prefix_cache seems involved, shuffle helps — suggests some cached prefix kv alignment bug under quant
sam: OK, next triage steps: (1) reproduce on same node (lee), (2) run kernel-level debug with qconfig logging for the attention op (maya+sam), (3) check tokenizer parity (sam), (4) confirm bootstrap significance on full cohort (olivia)
lee: Spinning job now. Node id: r-infer-11. Will run float32 -> int8 -> int8+flags in sequence and attach logs
eval-bot: shadowbench-run queued (id=sb-18222). ETA ~12m. Report will include per-query delta and candidate rank swaps
maya: Thanks. If we confirm prefix cache interaction, we should consider a short-term config: disable prefix_cache for int8 models while we fix kernel. That keeps production safe and buys time
olivia: Agree. I'll prepare a canary config to flip for dedicated and hosted int8 routes if needed (low blast radius)
sam: Also file a small regression test: seed + small curated set of 200 queries containing edge anchor lengths and priming templates; fail the build if ndcg drop > 0.02 vs float baseline
maya: I'll draft the test and upload sample set to /mnt/eval/triage_edge_anchors.jsonl
lee: Job finished on r-infer-11: float32 NDCG@10=0.4211, int8=0.3940, int8+disable-prefix-cache=0.4167. Logs attached to sb-18222
maya: Matches. Can we get a per-op discrepancy trace? sam: I'll hook up qconfig and run a single long query with verbose trace tomorrow morning. For now let's plan: rollback gate = disable int8 prefix_cache; owner: olivia to prepare canary; sam/maya to dig kernel.
maya: Assigning follow-ups: sam (kernel trace), lee (parity runs on 2 more nodes), olivia (canary rollout plan), maya (regression test + triage dataset)
maya: Tagging @here since it affects int8 bring-up schedule :eyes:
lee: noted :+1:
